A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeqWM and retain matching methods, benchmarks, and physical-robot experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v3 create specific interpretive uncertainty, rather than missing evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation results, model-prediction and component ablations, scalability experiments, timing measurements, and physical-robot demonstrations.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark and physical-robot results and reports additional intention-sharing ablations on Gate and PushBox.

M1.justification: V3 Eq. (2) specifies action-only messages, whereas v1 generally sends latent states and actions, reserving action-only communication for Cheetah. However, v3 Appendix A.1 and Algorithm 2 still specify both. Its new nonblocking execution description also elaborates an existing cache. These inconsistencies prevent reliably distinguishing an actual procedural revision from changed documentation.

E1.justification: V3 removes the MA-MuJoCo 6a-Cheetah evaluation and the three- and four-robot Gate scenarios, substantially narrowing reported domain and team coverage. The six Bi-DexHands tasks, three principal Multi-Quad tasks, physical deployments, and five-robot Gate demonstration remain; moving five benchmark curves into Appendix C.1 adds no coverage.

E2.justification: HASAC, MAT, MARIE, and MAPPO remain the principal benchmark comparators. V3 adds Gate/PushBox comparisons against DecWM and SeqFree. V1's six-task Planner-Only/Actor-Only comparison table disappears, although an actor-only endpoint remains in the timing analysis.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled Gate/PushBox comparisons that separately remove trajectory exchange or world modeling and restrict communication to single-step messages. Existing benchmark metrics, planner hyperparameters, prediction-error sampling/training budgets, and physical deployment settings remain unchanged. The new controls do not establish that retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds intention-sharing ablations on Gate and PushBox but removes the six-task actor/planner ablation table, quantitative team-size scaling analysis, critic-scale diagnostic, and several behavioral case studies. Prediction-accuracy, communication-fusion, smoothing, and early-stopping analyses remain. This substantially changes the supporting analysis portfolio.

E5.justification: Both versions describe benchmark curves as means over multiple seeds with 95% confidence intervals, without specifying seed counts. No changed repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented. Removing the actor-ablation table removes results, rather than establishing a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Gate/PushBox ablation curves favor SeqWM over DecWM and SeqFree, while Cheetah, quantitative team-scaling, and six-task actor/planner results are removed. The nine principal benchmark curves are retained across v3 Figures 3 and 12. The reported early-stopping time saving changes from 27.3% to 57.3% despite an unchanged timing plot; the five-robot passage-order description is also corrected.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix A.3 adds an approximate latency relation, Tstep ≈ max_i TMPPI(i) + Tcomm, and an O(1) scaling argument. V1's communication-complexity comparison and explicit normalization, target-encoding, and percentile-scaling mathematics are omitted. The principal learning and planning objectives remain, and neither version supplies a theorem-and-proof treatment.

C1.justification: V3 removes the headline linear-communication-overhead claim from the abstract and introduction and drops overhead reduction from the contribution list. It emphasizes modeling complexity and physical cooperation instead. The central sequential-model, intention-sharing, benchmark-performance, sample-efficiency, and sim-to-real claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds specific limitations concerning shared-reward cooperation and fixed/random agent ordering, plus proposed heterogeneous-team and human–robot extensions. It newly interprets DecWM/SeqFree results as demonstrating the necessity of prediction and intention exchange, and explains caches as avoiding serial blocking. These extend the largely retained coordination-mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: V3 removes network widths, layer configurations, parameter counts, Mish/SEM details, and two-hot, symlog, and percentile-scaling documentation from v1 Appendix B. Hyperparameter tables and physical setup details remain; cache-execution details and a reproducibility statement are added. The advertised repository target changes from seqwm-marl to seqwm. These are documentation changes, not proof that omitted components were removed from implementation.

R1.justification: V3 shifts decoder-free modeling attribution from Hafner et al. to Hansen et al. (2022), adds World4RL and Zhao et al. references, and removes MACD, A2PO, and several implementation-related citations. The broad positioning around centralized, decentralized, and sequential approaches remains.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract, introductory positioning, and behavioral explanations; promotes five-agent scalability into the main experimental narrative; and substantially reorganizes Appendices B–C. It also adds limitations, future work, ethics, reproducibility, and language-model-use statements. This is substantial narrative and structural reorganization.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 4 is split between v3 Figures 3 and 12, the paradigm schematic is redrawn and moved into the introduction, and five-robot behavior moves into the main text. V3 adds cache and ablation displays while removing communication-complexity, architecture, and actor-ablation tables and several supplementary visualizations. These substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 benefits from intention-sharing ablations, explicit limitations, and a corrected timing statement. However, it removes important architecture and normalization specifications and quantitative scalability evidence. Its action-only Eq. (2) also conflicts with Appendix A.1 and Algorithm 2, obscuring the evaluated communication mechanism. With the main benchmark evidence largely unchanged, these reproducibility and consistency losses outweigh the limited gains.
